title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing
claim: Editor-compiled catalogue. Vocabulary: additionally, delve, crucial, pivotal, showcase, tapestry, testament, underscore, vibrant, enduring, garner, intricate, interplay, landscape, meticulous, robust, fostering, highlight. Lists shift by era ('delve' peaked 2023-early 2024). One or two words are coincidence; many together is the signal.
example: stands as a counter-symbol, emphasizing unity, togetherness, and transcendent faith
fix: Do not 'fix' by swapping surface words without fixing the underlying vagueness.

title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing (copula avoidance)
claim: Copulative avoidance: 'serves as / stands as / marks / functions as / boasts / features' where 'is' / 'has' would do.
example: 'is LAAA's exhibition arm' became 'serves as LAAA's exhibition space'

title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing (negative parallelism)
claim: Negative parallelism: 'Not only ... but ...', 'It is not just ..., it's ...', 'no ..., no ..., just ...', 'Y rather than X'.
example: The issue here isn't just sourcing—it's framing.
fix: State the claim directly and drop the contrast: 'Chiang relied on military force to bring holdouts under control.'

title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing (rule of three, -ing tails, closers)
claim: Rule of three used to look comprehensive; sentences end in participial tails (highlighting/reflecting/emphasizing X); sections end in a vague positive or forward-looking closer; title-case headings; vague attribution ('Experts argue'); promotional diction (nestled, vibrant, rich, profound).
example: resilience, cultural richness, and natural beauty; ...reflecting its continued relevance in the regional and national transportation landscape.
fix: Keep only items that are supported (a list of two, or one point); sentence-case headings; cut the tail clause.

title: Sam Paech slop-forensics word and trigram lists (EQ-Bench slop score)
claim: Statistically over-represented words/trigrams vs human text across 10 models on story/essay prompts (1000 words list). Fiction trigram tells are stock body beats and scene furniture. Names are a big share of the word list (elara, aris, alaric, aeliana, aethel*, anya...). Also in word list: ashen, ashwood, whisper(ed/s), flickered, faintly, lingered, rustled, cacophony, bustling, calloused, ached, acrid, bated, arcane. Not in list: ash, ember, dust, hung, silence, weight (tested; probe could return hits, e.g. ashen). EQ-Bench slop score weights: words 45%, 'not X, but Y' contrasts 40%, trigrams 15% (earlier 60/25/15).
example: voice barely whisper; took deep breath; heart pounding chest; casting long shadows; sun dipped horizon; days turned weeks; chill run spine; breath caught throat; words hung air; air thick scent; dust motes danced; something else entirely; door creaked open; eyes never leaving; felt like eternity; room fell silent
fix: Per source: down-weight in sampling; for human editing, replace stock beat with a specific, scene-particular detail.

title: EQ-Bench Slop Score
claim: Slop score is a composite of overused words, 'not X, but Y' contrast patterns, and overused trigrams. Contrast pattern was weighted heavily (25-40%), i.e. treated as a top tell.

title: Kobak et al. excess vocabulary (Science Advances 2025)
claim: Excess-word analysis on 15M PubMed abstracts: 2024 excess words are mostly style words (66% verbs, 16% adjectives of 319). Ratios: delves 28.0x, underscores 13.8x, showcasing 10.7x; potential and crucial up in absolute share. At least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts LLM-processed. Academic register, not fiction.

title: Max Read repost: 'Dr. Elara Voss' as LLM archetype
claim: Almost any LLM asked for sci-fi names the lead 'Elara Voss' (or Elara Vex, Elena Voss, Elias Vance); no such character in books before 2023; appears in GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek, Grok; Gemma used Elara 39 times in 3 stories. Suggested cause: shared training corpus, WoW wiki gravity. Claude-specific frequency not documented here.
example: Elara Voss, physicist on the verge of a discovery, 'Erebus' project
fix: Choose names from an outside source (real name lists, region-appropriate), not the model.

title: The AI-isms of Writing-Bible (community Google Doc)
claim: Fiction-specific list with severity: em dashes (5), delve-type connectors, metaphor cliches (4), 'not X but Y' (4), rhetorical Q&A (4), rule of three (5), dramatic fragments (3), redundant adjective pairs (3), unmotivated metaphors added when asked to be 'descriptive' (5), telling after showing (4), 'too clean' prose (4).
example: What did she feel? Everything and nothing. / She waited. And waited. Nothing happened. / dark and brooding / a symphony of colors / a delicate balance / He stopped, he stared, he listened.
fix: Commas or periods for dashes (about one per 500 words); concrete description for stock metaphors; keep either the question or the answer; vary list lengths and sentence lengths; delete metaphors that do not clarify.

title: tropes.fyi: Negative parallelism
claim: Described as the most commonly identified AI tell; one use can work, many read as an insult. Variants include causal 'not because X but because Y' and the fragment pair.
example: It's not bold. It's backwards. / Retrofit it in a month. Not a decade. / So the post did not fail. It reached the people it could reach.
fix: Page gives no fix; Wikipedia's: state Y directly.

title: Sindome forum: AI generated writing (game community)
claim: Text-game players call out AI text as: vague overly wordy description, em dashes, 'It's not X. It's Y.', clichés and lists of three, polished lines with no human voice. Players note style alone is not proof.
example: On these cut-throat neon streets, a solo isn't just another murderer or anonymous shroud. He's an instigator of conflict.
fix: Cut vague filler; add concrete details only that character would notice; vary sentence structure; read aloud.

title: itch.io threads accusing games of AI text
claim: itch.io commenters flag descriptions by GPT-style formatting and frequent em dashes, and a shift in style between scenes (intro dialogue/metaphors vs the rest) as the tell; others push back that em dashes alone prove nothing. Anecdotal.

title: NC Bench 'Bad Writing Habits' (Claude models)
claim: Benchmark scores AI-ism words, adverbs, character and location names, filter words, purple prose, cliches. Claude Opus 4 / 3.7 Sonnet scored 100% on the AI-ism character-name check in one scenario but low (63%, 41%) on AI-ism word frequency: word-level tics, not names, were Claude's measurable weakness there. Name lists not visible.

title: Searches for Claude-specific tics, *-fall titles, 'something shifted'
claim: NULL: no source found documenting Claude-specific tics beyond the shared lists, nor documenting stock titles of the *-fall kind, nor 'something shifted' as a tell. Title clichés ('Whispers of', 'Echoes of') appear only in title-generator marketing, not as measured tells. The reviewer's *-fall claim is unsupported by what I found.
